name: frame-tools
summary: two generic tools for the raw frame streams of the handoff convention: frame-gen writes a synthetic pattern stream and frame-cmp compares two streams exactly, as bit patterns, at tolerance 0; neither computes any image operation

binaries.name: frame-gen
binaries.arguments: --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 --frames N [--fps N/D] [--pattern SPEC]; --help prints the usage on standard output and exits 0
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on a failure

binaries.name: frame-cmp
binaries.arguments: --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 [--fps N/D] [--frames N] [-v] A B; A and B are files, and one of them may be - for standard input; --help prints the usage on standard output and exits 0
binaries.stdin: read only when A or B is -
binaries.stdout: the report; with -v one line per frame present in both streams first
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0 and 1; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on exit 2, 3 and 4

frame_contract: frames/1 and frames/2 raw frames: depth 8 is packed rgba (4 bytes per pixel), depth 16 is packed rgba64le (8 bytes), depth 32 is planar gbrapf32le (16 bytes, planes G, B, R, A, 1.0 is full scale); whole frames back to back, no header, no padding, straight alpha, a frame of at most 4 GiB; a stream that ends inside a frame is a partial frame

patterns.meaning: every pixel has the four levels given, each 0 to 65535 with 65535 as full scale
R, G and B ramp from level 0 at the first column to 65535 at the last, A is full
square cells of the given size, black and white, A full; the colours swap on every frame
every sample is a draw of SplitMix64 seeded from the seed and the frame index
R, G, B are the levels 49152, 32768, 16384 and A ramps along the columns

level_mapping: depth 8: (level * 255 + 32767) / 65535 with integer division; depth 16: the level; depth 32: level / 65535 as a float
comparison: tolerance 0 on bit patterns: at depth 32 negative zero differs from zero, NaNs with different payloads differ and NaNs with one bit pattern are equal; the first difference is the first in frame order, then row, column and channel R, G, B, A
report: equal: equal frames=N width=W height=H depth=D; differ: differ frames_a=A frames_b=B compared=C equal=E different=F samples=S, then first frame=I x=X y=Y channel=R|G|B|A a=VALUE b=VALUE, or first none when only the frame counts differ; a value is decimal at depth 8 and 16 and FLOAT:BITS at depth 32 (the float in Rust debug form, the bit pattern in eight hex digits)
error_line: error: CODE: MESSAGE, where CODE is usage, unsupported, bad_input, partial_frame or broken_pipe
exit_one: frame-cmp exits 1 when the streams differ. The exit table of the convention gives 1 to stage_failed, which these tools never report, so 1 is free; it is the status that diff and cmp give for a difference, and a script can tell a difference (1) from a failure (2, 3, 4). frame-gen never exits 1

exit_codes_table.means: success, or frame-cmp found the streams equal
frame-cmp only: the streams differ (nothing failed)
exit_codes_table.table: a choice of the tool, see exit_one

exit_codes_table.means: unsupported: a depth other than 8, 16 or 32, or a frame over 4 GiB
bad_input: unreadable input, partial_frame, a declared frame count not met, or broken_pipe on standard output
exit_codes_table.table: the table's bad_input, partial_frame and broken_pipe
